method: Page fetched directly with curl and converted from HTML to text. Every claim is verbatim-checked against that file with scripts/verify.py. Prose paraphrases; source_text stays verbatim. The ondansetron weight-band table is a table rendered as text, quoted as one contiguous block; column alignment is a transcription risk and should be confirmed against the page before prescribing. Route, frequency and maximum for ondansetron are not stated on the page and are not reconstructed.

claims.claim: Bilious vomiting is obstruction until proven otherwise and needs urgent surgical referral
claims.source_text: Bilious (green) vomiting is due to a gastrointestinal obstruction until proven otherwise, and requires urgent surgical referral

claims.claim: Without diarrhoea consider causes other than gastroenteritis
claims.source_text: In a vomiting child without diarrhoea, always consider causes other than gastroenteritis

claims.claim: Always consider intracranial causes including inflicted injury
claims.source_text: Intracranial causes, including raised intracranial pressure (ICP) and inflicted injury, should always be considered

claims.claim: Cessation of vomiting does not exclude a serious cause
claims.source_text: Ondansetron can be used for symptomatic relief; however, cessation of vomiting does not exclude a serious cause

claims.claim: Vomiting is a symptom not a diagnosis and infection is the commonest cause
claims.source_text: Vomiting is a common and non-specific symptom, not a diagnosis … Infection is the most common cause of acute vomiting

claims.claim: Bile is dark green not yellow and a visual aid helps families
claims.source_text: Bile is dark green rather than yellow. Using a visual aid to clarify vomitus colour with families is helpful

claims.claim: Early morning vomiting with headache may be raised ICP
claims.source_text: Early morning vomiting and headache may be due to raised ICP

Bilious (dark green) … GIT obstruction … Swallowed blood eg epistaxis, or in neonate from maternal blood due to delivery or nipple trauma … Projectile … Pyloric stenosis … Early morning vomiting … Raised ICP
Wheeze, stridor, rash, cough, chest pain … Abdominal distension and tenderness, "tinkling"/absence of bowel sounds … Abdominal tenderness and fever
Lower abdominal/pelvic pain or testicular pain … Testicular torsion
Associated with certain food ingestion … Non-IgE mediated food allergy … Rectal bleeding … Intussusception
Fever or systemic illness … Meningitis … History of head injury/concern for NAI … Intracranial bleed
Abdominal pain, polyuria, polydipsia … Toxidromes, possible toxin ingestion, drug use … Cannabis hyperemesis … Consider inborn errors of metabolism

claims.claim: Other associations including pregnancy and eating disorders
claims.source_text: Specific pattern of vomiting … Cyclical vomiting syndrome … Urinary frequency, body changes, sexually active … Induced vomiting/purging, signs of disordered eating

Abdominal distension could suggest acute abdomen or bowel obstruction (ask parent if abdomen changed in appearance) … 'Tinkling' high-pitched or absent of bowel sounds may suggest gastrointestinal obstruction … Examine testes for torsion, particularly in adolescent boys
Altered conscious state and/or abnormal neurology (eg Cushing's triad) may suggest intracranial pathology … Bulging fontanelle may be a sign of raised ICP

Bilious vomiting … Lethargy or listlessness … Inconsolable +/- bulging fontanelle in infant … Neck stiffness, photophobia and fever in older child … Signs of peritonitis … Persistent vomiting with poor growth or abnormal development

claims.claim: Most well children with isolated vomiting need no investigations
claims.source_text: Most well children with isolated vomiting do not require any other investigations … Targeted investigation is directed by likely differential diagnoses
Consider BGL and ketones if BGL <3 mmol/L or >11 mmol/L. Ketotic hypoglycaemia can be a consequence of vomiting, more commonly in younger children
Treat shock with a bolus of 10-20 mL/kg sodium chloride 0.9% … If BGL <2.6 mmol/L, treat as per hypoglycaemia … If ketones present, consider carbohydrate source to correct (eg apple juice)
Consult local surgical team if there is evidence of a surgical cause of vomiting eg bowel obstruction, testicular or ovarian torsion and appendicitis
To assist with maintaining hydration in children >6 months of age
Weight Dose 8-15 kg 2 mg 15-30 kg 4 mg >30 kg 8 mg

claims.claim: Ondansetron may be given after head injury with monitoring
claims.source_text: Can be given with vomiting due to head injury provided other signs such as conscious state are carefully monitored
If ondansetron is ineffective, consult senior advice before prescribing other anti-emetics due to side effects

claims.claim: Oral rehydration first line including diluted apple juice
claims.source_text: Encourage oral fluids as a first line option eg oral rehydration solution or diluted apple juice (1:1 apple juice to water)
Advice regarding escalation of care … Patient is acutely unwell and not responding to fluid resuscitation … Severe metabolic derangement … Diagnostic uncertainty

Alert and able to tolerate small amounts of oral intake … Normal vital signs … The cause of vomiting has been identified and adequately managed … High risk diagnoses have been considered and there is an adequate follow up plan in place with clear instructions on when to seek earlier review
Last updated September 2025
